name: Greenness from space
summary: How green the land around each city is (NDVI, about 0 to 1) from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS satellites, in 250 to 500 m pixels, one value every 16 days.

el.name: Πρασινάδα από το διάστημα
el.summary: Πόσο πράσινη είναι η γη γύρω από κάθε πόλη (NDVI, περίπου 0 έως 1), από τους δορυφόρους MODIS και VIIRS της NASA, σε εικονοστοιχεία 250 έως 500 m, μία τιμή κάθε 16 ημέρες.

publisher.name: NASA (MODIS and VIIRS land products, LP DAAC); subsets by ORNL DAAC

licence.attribution: NASA MODIS/VIIRS land products (LP DAAC), subset by ORNL DAAC TESViS, doi:10.3334/ORNLDAAC/1600

restrictions: ORNL DAAC asks users to cite both the subset tool (TESViS) and the product
The documentation we read gives no rate limit: we ask a few times a day, one call at a time

coverage.area: Global land (we read the four city centres)

update.note: One composite per 16-day period; Terra and Aqua are 8 days apart. We check twice a day.

variables.note: Greenness score, about 0 (bare) to 1 (dense green). Not a tree count.

quality.uncertainty: A 16-day composite of the clearest days. Mixed city pixels (roofs, gardens, sea) blur the score; small parks and single trees do not show.
known_issues: NDVI says how green the surface is, not how many trees there are: dry summer grass and green crops score very differently
A pixel is 250 to 500 m wide and mixes roofs, roads, gardens and sometimes sea: it is an area, not a spot at the school
Cloudy, snowy and shadowed pixels are thrown out; in a cloudy period the value can be a month old
Terra and Aqua (MODIS) are drifting off their orbits and NASA plans to retire both from late 2026 or early 2027; VIIRS carries on

upstream.name: NASA MODIS vegetation indices 16-day (MOD13Q1, MYD13Q1) and VIIRS vegetation indices 16-day (VNP13A1)

use_for: Saying how green or bare the land around a city is, and how that changes through the year
A hint about why a nearby area may be hotter or cooler
not_for: Counting trees or measuring the shade of one school yard
Saying a park is healthy or unhealthy

notes: Built from the ORNL DAAC documentation (modis.ornl.gov/rst/api/v1: /dates and /subset, no key); not tested against the live service from our build sandbox. Compare it with osm-green-space (a planned share of mapped parks and trees): they should roughly agree, but NDVI also sees gardens and weeds nobody mapped and misses small trees inside a pixel full of roofs. Pair it with modis-lst: greener ground is usually cooler.
